svg.title: Exact basis rotation, dephasing, and truncation are different operations
svg.desc: An algebraic one-electron example starts from c=(sqrt(0.6),sqrt(0.3),sqrt(0.1)) and rho=c c-transpose. A real orthogonal pi-over-six rotation mixes basis vectors one and two. The transformed matrix U-transpose rho U still has trace one and purity one. Dephasing in the new basis keeps diagonal entries approximately 0.89242346,0.00757654,0.1 but removes all off-diagonal entries; trace stays one and purity becomes 0.80647704. Retaining only basis vectors one and two gives P D P with trace 0.9. It is not renormalized; the omitted trace is 0.1. All matrix entries in this example are nonnegative and share one zero-to-one color scale. Numbers are rounded to three decimals. The outlined two-by-two block is retained; gray cells are omitted. These basis vectors are not claimed to be a physical subband calculation.
svg.text: Gray cells omitted; outlined block retained.
